record.paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
record.original_question: Is it true that every simple graph G on n vertices satisfies λ1(G) + λ1(Ḡ) ≤ (4/3)n − 5/3 minus the residue-class correction stated in the source, namely f1(n) when n mod 3 = 1, 0 when n mod 3 = 2, and f2(n) when n mod 3 = 0, where f1(n) = (3n − 2 − sqrt(9n^2 − 12n + 12))/6 and f2(n) = (3n − 1 − sqrt(9n^2 − 6n + 9))/6? If so, are the equality cases exactly the graphs G or complements Ḡ that are complete split graphs whose independent set has size floor(n/3), and also size ceil(n/3) when n mod 3 = 2?

evidence.page: Nordhaus–Gaddum inequality for the spectral radius, HTML lines 1208-1212
evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.1... For any simple graph G, with complement Ḡ, index λ1(G) and n vertices we have λ1(G) + λ1(Ḡ) ≤ 4/3 n - 5/3 - { ... } ... This bound is sharp and attained if and only if G or Ḡ is a complete split graph with an independent set on ⌊n/3⌋ vertices (and also on ⌈n/3⌉ vertices if n mod(3) = 2).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a simple graph on n vertices, let Ḡ denote its complement, and let λ₁(H) denote the spectral radius (largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix) of a graph H. Define
  f₁(n) = (3n − 2 − √(9n² − 12n + 12))/6,
  f₂(n) = (3n − 1 − √(9n² − 6n + 9))/6,
and the residue-class correction
  c(n) = f₁(n) if n ≡ 1 (mod 3),
  c(n) = 0     if n ≡ 2 (mod 3),
  c(n) = f₂(n) if n ≡ 0 (mod 3).
A complete split graph CS(n,k) is the graph on n vertices obtained as the join of a clique on n−k vertices and an independent set on k vertices.

(a) Prove or disprove: for every simple graph G on n vertices,
   λ₁(G) + λ₁(Ḡ) ≤ (4n − 5)/3 − c(n).

(b) If the inequality in (a) holds, determine whether equality is attained exactly when G or Ḡ is isomorphic to a complete split graph CS(n, ⌊n/3⌋), with the additional case CS(n, ⌈n/3⌉) when n ≡ 2 (mod 3).
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 preprint (arXiv:2506.11401) proves the conjecture, identifying the extremal graphs that maximize λ₁(G)+λ₁(Ḡ) as the complete split graphs K_{⌊n/3⌋} ∨ N_{⌈2n/3⌉} (with a secondary case when n ≡ 2 mod 3), thereby resolving the 2007 Nordhaus–Gaddum-type conjecture on the spectral radius for all n ≥ 3 via linear-algebraic techniques building on Csikvári's staircase structure.

status_evidence.title: Nordhaus-Gaddum inequality for the spectral radius of a graph of order n
status_evidence.snippet: Resolves the 2007 conjecture by determining the extremal graphs maximizing ρ(G)+ρ(Ḡ) as complete split graphs K_{⌊n/3⌋} ∨ N_{⌈2n/3⌉}.
status_evidence.claim: The conjectured Nordhaus–Gaddum bound and equality cases for the spectral radius are established.
